This report presents the masterplan outcomes and concept planning process undertaken for the proposed St Clair Community Facility and the St Clair Recreation Precinct Parking Study. It provides an overview of the project scope, concept designs, indicative cost estimates, stakeholder engagement activities, and proposed next steps arising from this work.

In line with Council’s resolution of 25 November 2024 (CL 25/11/24, Item 6.110), which endorsed the preparation of a precinct-wide master plan to guide future funding, staging, and implementation, this report recommends that Council endorse both the Community Facility concept design and the parking design contained within the Parking Study for inclusion as budget bids in the 2026/27 Annual Business Plan and Budget process.


The report also notes that staff will continue to actively pursue external funding and partnership opportunities to assist with delivery of the endorsed projects. In addition, it seeks Council approval to proceed with community engagement on a proposed game day retractable boundary fence at St Clair Oval 2 - an adaptable design that meets Football South Australia Premier League competition standards while maintaining full open community access when games are not being played.




Moved: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan
Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

That Council:
 
  1. Endorses the St Clair Recreation Precinct Parking Study (Appendix 1), including the proposed parking design, for inclusion as a budget bid in the 2026/27 Annual Business Plan and Budget process.
 
  1. Endorses the St Clair Community Facility concept design (Appendix 2) for inclusion as a budget bid in the 2026/27 Annual Business Plan and Budget process.
 
  1. Notes that Council staff will continue to actively pursue external funding and partnership opportunities to assist with delivery and funding of the endorsed projects.
 
  1. Approves the Community Engagement Approach (Appendix 5) to seek community feedback on the proposed game day retractable boundary fencing, designed to meet Football South Australia Premier League competition standards while maintaining open community access outside of scheduled games at St Clair Oval 2. 
 
  1. Requests that the outcomes of community consultation be presented to Council following the conclusion of the engagement period.

Carried 

 Division called by Councillor - Kelly Thomas

The City of Charles Sturt must release an updated Disability Access and Inclusion Plan (DAIP) by 14 February 2026 under the Disability Inclusion Act 2018. A draft Plan has been prepared to align with the new State Disability Inclusion Plan 2025–2029, attached to this report. It has been written in simple, accessible language to ensure it can be widely read and understood. We will also make consultation information available in other formats, including Easy Read.

The DAIP is our strategic commitment to creating an inclusive city where all residents can participate fully in community life. The plan was developed through extensive consultation with people with disability and their families and carers, and other community members and stakeholders. This engagement directly shaped the plan's 57 actions to be delivered from 2026 to 2030. Great care has been taken to ensure that the draft DAIP reflects the feedback from our community.

The draft plan reflects feedback gathered during the first stage of community engagement, in line with the endorsed CEA. Council approval is sought for the draft plan, which will then be shared with the community in line with the second stage of the endorsed CEA.



Moved: Councillor Katriona Kinsella
Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

  1. That Council approves the draft DAIP to be released for Stage 2 consultation as detailed in the endorsed Community Engagement Approach (refer CL 10/06/25, Item 6.40).

Councillor Peter Ppiros entered the meeting at 7:50 PM.
Carried Unanimously

This report provides Council with an opportunity to consider an Unsolicited Proposal in accordance with Council’s Unsolicited Proposals Policy (adopted 9 October 2023 and in line with the revised Policy subject to Council's endorsement on 10 November 2025).

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b) as the information where the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.



Moved: Councillor George Turelli
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Recommendation - Exclusion of the Public (from 8:09 PM)

That:
  1. Pursuant to Section 90(2) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council hereby orders that the public be excluded from attendance at this meeting, with the exception of the Chief Executive Officer, General Manager City Futures, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager City Operations, Acting General Manager Engaged Community, Manager Financial Services, Manager Strategic Procurement Services, Manager City Property and Open Space, Acting Manager Governance and Risk, Acting Manager City Planning and Sustainability, Governance Officer, Lester Mackenzie (President - Grange Bowling Club), Aaron Halliday (Vice President - Grange Bowling Club), and Neil Comben (Board Member - Grange Bowling Club) currently in attendance at the meeting, in order to consider ITEM 11.1 - UNSOLICITED PROPOSAL - COUNCIL DECISION TO PROCEED in confidence.

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 11.1 - UNSOLICITED PROPOSAL - COUNCIL DECISION TO PROCEED on the following grounds:

b.
information where the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.
Carried Unanimously

Councillor - Nicole Mazeika left the meeting at 8:30 PM.
Councillor - Nicole Mazeika left the meeting at 8:32 PM.


Moved: Councillor Rachele Tullio
Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion


That Council:

 

  1. Acknowledges the importance of providing open space for the City of Charles Sturt community.

 

  1. Endorses the progression of the unsolicited proposal from the Grange Bowling Club from Stage 1 (Initial Proposal) to Stage 2 (Detailed Proposal), in accordance with Council’s Unsolicited Proposal Policy.

 

  1. Notes that the preparation of the Stage 2 detailed proposal will be undertaken by Council staff, with any required professional services costs to be funded by the Grange Bowling Club.

 

  1. Delegates to the Chief Executive Officer the authority to negotiate and prepare a Stage 2 detailed proposal with reference to the following guiding principles:

 

  1. The proposal delivers a broader community benefit, including opportunities to improve or redevelop the Grange Bowling Club facilities and/or membership arrangements in a manner that enables the co-location or consolidation of compatible community or sporting clubs, optimises community access to open space, and reduces pressure on limited open-space assets;

 

  1. The proposal represents the best possible value for money for Council and the community and minimises the impact on rates, acknowledging that the proponent’s initial offer is an ambit position, and providing for negotiation of price and terms, including the structure and duration of any future lease arrangements;

  2. The proposal is financially sound, including consideration of mechanisms such as negotiation, partial land annexation or disposal to offset redevelopment costs, and the long-term operational sustainability of the facility; and

  3. The proposal aligns with Council’s strategic objectives for open space, asset management, and community wellbeing.

  

  1. Requires that, prior to any binding commitment being entered into:

 

  • A prudential review under section 48 of the Local Government Act 1999 be considered by Council’s Audit and Risk Committee; and

 

  • The final Stage 2 proposal and prudential review be presented to Council for final consideration and decision.

 

  1. Approves the reimbursement of the Grange Bowling Club for any professional services costs incurred (currently estimated at approximately $20,000) in the event that a detailed proposal is not ultimately accepted, with reimbursement to be funded from the recurrent operating budget.

  2. That Council thank the presenters from the Grange Bowling Club and that the presentation and notes provided by the Grange Bowling Club be included in the Minutes.

  3. That ITEM 11.1 - UNSOLICITED PROPOSAL - COUNCIL DECISION TO PROCEED having been considered in confidence pursuant to Section 90(3)(b) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Council hereby orders, in accordance with Section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999 that the report, appendix, and the minutes of this item be kept confidential until all conveyancing transactions to transfer ownership have been finalised and new ownership title issued, or until the proposal is ultimately unsuccessful.
Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 17 November 2025.


Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Quin Tran

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Item 4.1 and 4.3:

 

4.2. - PRESENTATION AND REPORT - RENEWAL SA SEATON MASTERPLAN AND INFRASTRUCTURE FUNDING
 
Motion 
 
 That the Strategic and Engagement Committee recommends that Council:
 
  1. Note the Seaton Masterplan prepared by Renewal SA, which outlines the planned redevelopment of land within Seaton.
 
  1. Acknowledge that elements of the masterplan affecting Council-managed land will be subject to separate statutory processes, community consultation and future Council decisions before any implementation occurs, including (but not limited to) matters under the Roads (Opening and Closing) Act 1991, the Local Government Act 1999, or any other relevant legislative requirements.
 
  1. Endorse the preparation of:
    • an application to the Minister for Transport for a 40 km/h Area Speed Limit within the Seaton development precinct; and
    • an application to PLEC for the undergrounding of powerlines in key locations consistent with the updated masterplan.
 
  1. Endorse the inclusion of a budget bid in the 2026/27 budget process for a $680,000 contribution towards infrastructure and public-realm upgrades associated with Stages 2 and 3 of the Seaton Project, and the inclusion of an annual allocation of $325,000 in the Long-Term Financial Plan from 2027/28 to 2035/36 to support future stages.
  
4.4. - COASTAL SOUNDS EVENT - REVIVE LIVE GRANT APPLICATION 
 
Motion 
 
  1. That Council acknowledges and accepts any potential grant offer received through the Federal Government's Revive Live grant program for the 2026 Coastal Sounds Festival.
 
4.5. - HISTORICAL SOCIETIES GRANTS PROGRAM
 
Motion
 
 1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the recommended grant allocations be endorsed as follows:
  1. Hindmarsh Historical Society - $2,370
  2. Charles Sturt Memorial Museum Trust - $9,240
  3. Henley & Grange Historical Society - $9,000
  4. Fort Glanville Historical Association - $5,700
  
4.6. - ROTARY WEST LAKES - OFFER OF FUNDING FOR IMPROVEMENTS AT MIDCOURSE RESERVE
 
Motion 
 
  1. That Council notes the letter from the Rotary Club of West Lakes included as Appendix 1.
 
  1. That Council considers allocating $25,000 in its 2026/27 budget towards the installation of a new shelter, picnic setting, drinking fountain and associated works at Midcourse Reserve, West Lakes, as part of a 50/50 funding arrangement with the Rotary Club of West Lakes.
 
  1. That Council writes to the Rotary Club of West Lakes, expressing appreciation for the offer of funding and advising of Council’s decision.
 
4.7. - APPOINTMENT OF ONE NEW MEMBER TO THE COUNCIL ASSESSMENT PANEL
 
Motion
 
  1. That it be recommended to Council that it appoints Henry Inat to the vacant independent Council Assessment Panel position for a two year term commencing 1 January 2026 and concluding on 31 December 2027.
 
9.1. - PRESENTATION - AGED CARE REFORMS - INFORMATION UPDATE
 
Motion
 
  1. That the presentation be received and noted.

  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

Leave the meeting was sought to hear a presentation from Council staff in relation to Item 4.1 - Presentation and Report - Seaton Code Amendment. Leave was granted.


Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

4.1. - PRESENTATION AND REPORT - SEATON CODE AMENDMENT
 
Motion
 
  1. That Committee recommends to Council that the submission provided in Appendix 1 be endorsed as Council's formal response to the Seaton Code Amendment, subject to the following amendments; 

     - Requesting a more detailed concept plan for the community as part of the consultation.
     - Stronger language in relation to the importance of setbacks in relation to building heights.
    -  Expressing opposition to the proposed 10-storey building height due to the excessive scale and visual impact on the surrounding neighbourhood, as well as the significant increase in population density it would generate in the west and the resulting negative impacts on traffic congestion and on-street parking availability. 
    -  That consideration of the Seaton Code Amendment is looked at in a more holistic manner, taking into account the cumulative impact of already approved developments as well as future potential development sites when making its decision.  
    -  Recognise and assess the expected increase in demand for local services, including schools, medical and allied health support, local sporting facilities, parks and open space, to ensure community are provided adequate living standards.

  1. That staff be thanked for their presentation and that the presentation also be provided at the council meeting.
Carried Unanimously

Moved: Councillor Katriona KinsellaSeconded: Councillor Kelly Thomas

4.3. - PRESENTATION AND REPORT - LOCAL COMMUNITY ACCESS TO SCHOOL OVALS
 
Motion 
 
  1. That Council includes a budget bid through the 2026/27 Annual Business Plan process to allocate $375,000 per site (total $750,000) for the delivery of two pilot Local Community Access School Ovals at Woodville High School and West Lakes Shore Primary School, to fund lighting and other supporting infrastructure enabling shared use for community sport and recreation outside school hours.
 
  1. That Council delegates authority to the Chief Executive Officer to negotiate and finalise Joint Use Agreements with the Department for Education and the governing bodies of Woodville High School and West Lakes Shore Primary School, ensuring suitable arrangements for access, maintenance responsibilities, cost-sharing and community benefit that prioritise local community use.
 
  1. That Council supports continued planning and engagement to identify and progress further opportunities for Local Community Access School Ovals across the City, building on the interest and priorities identified through the recent community sport survey and early discussions with local stakeholders
 
  1. That Council adopts a formal advocacy position supporting a long-term program of Local Community Access School Ovals to unlock school facilities and alleviate pressure on Council’s parks and ovals and seeks State and Federal Government partnerships and other funding opportunities to co-invest in infrastructure that expands equitable access to open space for the local community.

  2. That staff be thanked for their presentation.

  3. That a report be brought to Council following the conclusion of the pilot and consideration of next strategic steps.
 
Carried Unanimously

The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 17 November 2025.


Moved: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan
Seconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1. - CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS
 
Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program or Annual Operating Program be approved and adjusted in the Financial Statements at the next quarterly review as they involve transfers between renewal and new/upgrade works and or new projects to be funded by unbudgeted income:-
     
     a. Budgeted expenditure for AMP Fences Walls and Bollards 25/26 (Renewal Project 3629) be increased by $450,000 from savings in the Gleneagles Reserve Stormwater Flood Mitigation and Reserve (Upgrade Project 3454).
     
     b. Budgeted expenditure for AMP Playground Renewals 9 individual projects be increased by;
      
    • The Westwood Reserve (Renewal Project - 3830) by $63,249
    • The Avenue Reserve -Shade Structure (Renewal Project 3853) by $29,448
    • Grange Recreation Reserve - East (Renewal Project 3828) by $57,623
    • Grange Recreation Reserve - West (Renewal Project 3829) by $54,064
    • Grange Recreation Reserve - Shade Structure (Renewal Project 3852) by $17,777
    • First Avenue Reserve (Renewal Project 3827) by $21,758
    • Croydon Reserve - Senior (Renewal Project 3825) by $14,039
    • Croydon Reserve – Junior (Renewal Project 3826) by $9,616
    • River Park Reserve - Playground (Renewal Project 3669) by $239,557
       
       totaling $507,130 from savings in the River Park Reserve - Path and Planting (Renewal Project 3670) $180,638 and Gleneagles Reserve Stormwater Flood Mitigation and Reserve (Upgrade Project 3454) $326,492.
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
     
     a. Budgeted expenditure for Road Rehabilitation Program 2025/26-Aberfeldy Avenue (Renewal Project - 3702) be increased by $725,000 from reallocation of existing project funds in the Road Reconstruction Program 2025/26-Napier Street (Renewal Project -3729). 
     
     b. Budgeted expenditure for Bus Stop 24 Seaview Road Renewal (Renewal Project 3697) be increased by $50,000 from savings in the Bus Stop 25 Seaview Road Renewal (Renewal Project 3698) $25,000 and Bus Stop 28 Seaview Road Renewal (Renewal Project 3699) $25,000.
     
     c. Budgeted expenditure for Flinders Park Tennis – Court & Lighting (Upgrade Project 3587) be increased by $29,929 from savings in the Gleneagles Reserve Stormwater Flood Mitigation and Reserve (Upgrade Project 3454). 

  2.  That by endorsing the variations listed in 1. above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.
 
4.2. - ST CLAIR RECREATION CENTRE QUARTERLY REPORT - JULY, AUGUST AND SEPTEMBER 2025 
 
 Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the YMCA's Performance Report for the July to September 2025 quarter. 
 
  1. That further quarterly reports be presented to the Operations Committee.
 
4.3. - STATE BICYCLE FUND GRANT ACCEPTANCE 25/26  
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council accepts a funding grant of $5,000 from the Department for Infrastructure and Transport’s State Bicycle Fund to contribute towards the concept design of a new wombat crossing on St Clair Avenue, between Tulloch Drive and Swans Place.
 
  1. That Council enters into a formal agreement with the Minister for Transport to secure the funding.
      
  2. That the Chief Executive Officer be authorised to sign the funding agreement to give effect to the above resolutions. 
 
4.4. - STREETSCAPE UPGRADE PROJECTS - QUARTERLY UPDATE REPORT
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted. 

  2. That quarterly updates on the Chief Street, Hawker Street and Renown Park Living Streets Streetscape Projects be presented to the Operations Committee.

  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

g.
matters that must be considered in confidence in order to ensure that the council does not breach any law, order or direction of a court or tribunal constituted by law, any duty of confidence, or other legal obligation or duty.

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.
Carried Unanimously

Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

This report presents the outcomes of a request from West Beach Parks to formally assign private road names and street numbering to properties along Military Road and West Beach Road, West Beach. The proposal seeks to resolve longstanding issues with wayfinding, emergency response, and mail delivery across both the City of Charles Sturt and City of West Torrens boundaries.

Moved: Councillor Tom Scheffler
Seconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Motion

  1. That the consultation approach of ‘inform’, as outlined in the Community Engagement Approach document (Appendix 1), be noted.
 
  1. That Council endorse the following properties within the City of Charles Sturt be assigned private road names. 
 
  • West Beach Tennis Club (SA Catholic Tennis Association) and St Michael and All Angels Netball Club be assigned the private road name 1 Sports Lane. 
  • Sport SA be assigned the private road name 3 Sports Lane.
  • West Beach Parks HQ and Sports Hub Offices be assigned the private road name 1 West Beach Lane. 
 
  1. That Council notes the Glenelg Lacrosse Club be assigned street numbering 23 West Beach Road.
 
  1. That Council notes the City of West Torrens as the adjoining Council supports the above recommendations.
 
  1. That, in line with the Road Naming and Premises Numbering Policy, notice of this Council resolution be given to relevant authorities in writing, to affected property owners/tenants, and to the public in the form of a public notice in the Government Gazette and a newspaper circulating within the state.

  2. That the City of Charles Sturt notes the following properties are within the City of West Torrens area and supports the following private road names and/or street numbering:

  • SAPOL Road Safety Centre – 1A Military Road
  • The Retreat at West Beach Parks – 1C Military Road
  • Westward Ho Golf Club  – 1 Golf Drive
  • The Pat G.C. - 2 Golf Drive
  • Baseball SA – 1/27 West Beach Road
  • Softball SA – 2/27 West Beach Road
  • The Studio – 3/27 West Beach Road
  • German Shepherd Dog Club of SA – 33 West Beach Road
  • West Beach Parks Football Centre – 41 West Beach Road 

  1. That Council provides the City of West Torrens with Council's decision.

Carried Unanimously

The Sam Johnson Reserve Clubroom Redevelopment is an important community project aimed at delivering modern, inclusive and functional sporting facilities. As the project has progressed, rising construction and site-related costs have created budget implications that exceed the current allocation. This report outlines the financial considerations, examines available delivery options and recommends a practical way forward to ensure the project can continue while managing impacts on future Council budgets and incorporating potential external funding opportunities.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Alice Campbell declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.7. The nature of Councillor - Alice Campbell's general conflict is that the report included in this item mentions SANFL as a possible funder of the project. Her partner is an employee of SANFL. Councillor - Alice Campbell dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and left the meeting. 

Councillor - Alice Campbell left the meeting at 8:03 PM.


Moved: Councillor Katriona KinsellaSeconded: Councillor Merlindie Fardone

Motion

  1. That Council endorse staff to submit a budget bid for the 2026/27 financial year to fully fund the Sam Johnson Reserve Clubroom Redevelopment project in a single stage.

  2. That Council endorse appointing the recommended building contractor in the 2025/26 financial year and commit to delivering the full upgrade in a single stage, thereby avoiding the need for a staged approach and preventing additional contractor mobilisation costs.

  3. That Council accept any successful external grant funding currently being sourced by the Fitzroy Community Club, the licence holder of the clubroom, with the intention of reducing the overall project cost to Council and adjusting the 2026/27 budget bid accordingly.


Carried Unanimously
Councillor - Alice Campbell entered the meeting at 8:05 PM.

This report presents the draft Regional Education Plan approved as a draft by the CAWRA Board.
 
Moved: Councillor Katriona Kinsella
Seconded: Councillor Tom Scheffler

Motion

  1. That Council receive and note the report, including the draft waste, recycling and circular economy education strategy titled 'Rethink Reset Recycle' which has been approved as a draft by the CAWRA Board for consideration by its two constituent Councils (Appendix 1).

    1. Educate the community in the correct use of kerbside bins.
    2. Undertake a major review of community waste and recycling education programs and design a comprehensive new education program for rollout from 2025 to 2030.
    3. Ensure staff and decision makers are trained and informed on current waste, recycling and circular economy issue.
 
  1. That Council endorse the proposed approach to further targeted stakeholder engagement as described in this report, including YourSay, with feedback from that process to be considered prior to providing a final strategy to the CAWRA Board and both councils for their adoption. 

  1. That Council agree that the draft strategy be used to inform Council’s 2026/27 Budget and Business Plan process.

Carried Unanimously

The purpose of this report is to seek Council endorsement of the proposed Community Engagement Approach to inform the development of the City of Charles Sturt Arts & Culture Plan.
 
The Community Engagement Approach outlines how Council will collaborate with the creative sector, stakeholders, and the broader community to develop a clear, contemporary, and actionable Arts & Culture Plan that aligns with Council’s Community Vision, City Plan, and relevant State and Federal policy frameworks.


Moved: Councillor Quin TranSeconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion

  1. That Council endorses the Community Engagement Approach outlined in Appendix 1 to seek community and industry feedback for the development of an Arts and Culture Plan.

  2. That Council notes that a draft Arts and Culture Plan will be developed through a two-stage Community Engagement Approach:
    1. Creative Sector, Creative Community & Stakeholder Engagement
    2. Community Engagement on the draft Arts and Culture Plan

  3. That Council notes that a draft Arts and Culture Plan will be presented to a future meeting of Council, incorporating feedback gathered through the Community Engagement Approach.

Carried Unanimously

The Event Grant and Event Sponsorship Policy, endorsed by Council in July 2025, supports the funding of events delivered by and within the community. This report seeks Council approval for a multi-year agreement of $10,000 per year for three years under the Community Event Fund grant to support the Vietnamese–Adelaide Tết Festival 2026, 2027 and 2028, delivered by the Vietnamese Community in Australia (SA Chapter Inc.) (VCASA).

While the event meets the eligibility criteria under the Policy, the application was received on 13 January 2026 for an event scheduled to be held on 7–8 February 2026. These dates fall outside the assessment timeframe for Round 2 of the Community Event Fund, which closes on 31 January 2026 and is considered through the standard panel, Committee and Council approval process.

As a result, consideration through the usual process would not occur until after the event has taken place. Accordingly, this report seeks early approval from Council to enable support for this long-running, well-regarded event, which is strongly supported by the community and holds significant cultural importance within the City of Charles Sturt.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Quin Tran declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.2. The nature of Councillor - Quin Tran's general conflict is that she is a volunteer member for Vietnamese Community in Australia (SA Chapter Inc) and Vietnamese Community School in SA. Councillor - Quin Tran dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.2 and not participating in the debate or vote.


Moved: Councillor Senthil ChidambaranathanSeconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Motion

  1. That Council approves a multi-year agreement of $10,000 per year for three years under the Community Event Fund grant to the Vietnamese Community in Australia (SA Chapter Inc.) to support the Vietnamese–Adelaide Tết Festival in 2026, 2027 and 2028, subject to the terms and conditions of the Event Grants and Event Sponsorship Funding Agreement.

  2. That Council notes that the application has been assessed and presented outside the standard Event Grants timeline, as the event is scheduled to occur prior to the completion of the current funding round assessment and subsequent consideration by the Strategic & Engagement Committee and Council.


Carried Unanimously

At the Ordinary Council meeting of 10 November 2025, Council was presented the masterplan outcomes and concept plans for the proposed St Clair Community Facility (CL 10/11/25, Item 6.2 St Clair Concept Design). 

Resolutions from this report included approval for the proposed Community Engagement Approach to seek community feedback on the proposed game day retractable boundary fencing, designed to meet Football South Australia Premier League competition standards while maintaining open community access outside of scheduled games at St Clair Oval No. 2. 

This report outlines the outcomes of the Community Engagement Approach undertaken in relation to the proposed fencing of this portion of St Clair Oval No. 2 and, having regard to the feedback received, seeks Council endorsement to incorporate the retractable boundary fencing into the St Clair Community Facility design.


Moved: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan
Seconded: Councillor Quin Tran

Motion

That Council:

  1. Acknowledge the findings of the Community Engagement Summary Report relating to the St Clair Oval No. 2 'Football South Australia - Competition Compliant' fencing, as detailed in Appendix 1.

  2. Endorse the St Clair Oval No. 2 fence design as detailed in Appendix 2, for inclusion in the St Clair Community Facility design.

  3. Note that a budget bid will be submitted in 2026/27 for a multi-year project, with the St Clair Community Facility building works funded/delivered in 2026/27, and the 'Football South Australia - Competition Compliant' fencing funded/delivered in 2027/28.


Carried

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

In line with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures, Mayor Evans has provided a report for the months of November and December 2025, detailing her activities, functions and media interactions in her official capacity.


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Motion

  1. That the report be received and noted and that the Mayor's notes relating to the Santos Tour Down Under, Library refuge due to extreme heat and response to missed bin collection are included in the Minutes.
Carried Unanimously

Mayor's Notes:
  1. The Tour Down Under event on Friday 23 January brought an incredible buzz to Henley Beach Square and surrounding areas, with an estimated 25,000 people coming through over the day. It was wonderful to see our community showcased at its very best. My sincere thanks go to Cat Conidi and her team for delivering such a successful event, supported by the Engaged Community Division and our organisation as a whole.
 
Both the Race Director from Santos and an Executive from the South Australian Tourism Commission praised the event, confirming this was the best attended Tour Down Under stage in its history. A fantastic achievement for everyone involved.
 
  1. I would also like to recognise the exceptional efforts of staff who coordinated the opening of our Civic Library as a cool and safe refuge during the extreme heat on Monday’s public holiday. This was a values-led decision reflected the care and responsiveness we aim to demonstrate as an organisation, especially on a day when many usual places of refuge were closed.
 
Special thanks also to the team who made this possible on the ground from the Engaged Community Division, supported by City Operations and City Futures.
 
  1. Finally, I’d like to acknowledge the strong community interest following the missed bin collections over the weekend. The update post reached more than 40,000 people, highlighting just how important timely communication is to our residents. Thank you to staff Georgia Borthwick and Sarah Kipling from Engaged Communities, who responded to enquiries throughout the weekend and helped keep our community informed during what was understandably a frustrating situation.

Brief

This report presents the final Detailed Proposal for the proposed amalgamation of the Grange Bowling Club and West Lakes Bowling Club, and the outcomes of Stage 2 investigations undertaken in accordance with Council’s Unsolicited Proposals Policy.

The Detailed Proposal outlines the proposed acquisition of the Grange Bowling Club land by the City of Charles Sturt, the amalgamation of the Grange Bowling Club and West Lakes Bowling Club into a single entity, relocation arrangements, redevelopment of the Grange site, and the proposed long-term tenure, maintenance and initial operating arrangements for the merged club.


The Detailed Proposal has been developed collaboratively between Council staff and the two bowling clubs. Council is now requested to note the Detailed Proposal and initiate a prudential review under Section 48 of the Local Government Act 1999, with the review to be considered by Council’s Audit and Risk Committee.


It is also noted that the future design process for Jubilee Reserve is contingent on the outcome of the proposed bowling club merger, on the basis that the bowling greens would no longer occupy the Jubilee site. This dependency reopens broader design possibilities for Jubilee Reserve and will be the subject of a separate future report.

 

Material Declaration of Interest

Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 6.4. The nature of Councillor van den Nieuwelaar's material conflict is that she has a relative who is a Member of the West Lakes Bowling Club and left the meeting.

Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar left the meeting at 8:00 PM.

Moved: Councillor Rachele TullioSeconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

That Council:

  1. Notes the Detailed Proposal developed in collaboration with the Grange and West Lakes Bowling Clubs (Appendix 1), and the proposed total Council financial contribution of $5,700,000 (excluding GST).

  2. Undertakes a prudential review under Section 48 of the Local Government Act 1999 and refers the prudential review to Council’s Audit and Risk Committee for consideration. 

  3. Receives a further report containing the prudential review findings and Audit and Risk Committee advice for Council’s consideration prior to determining whether to progress the proposal to Stage 3 (Negotiation and Approval) and make a Formal Offer to the Grange and West Lakes Bowling Clubs respectively.



Moved: Councillor Edgar AgiusSeconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

Motion

That the Motion be put.
Carried


The Motion to Item 6.4 was Carried 

Councillor Rachele Tullio left the meeting at 8:32 PM.

Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar entered the meeting at 8:33 PM.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Brief
The purpose of this report is to seek Council endorsement of the City of Charles Sturt Statement of Commitment to Closing the Gap in Western Adelaide, acknowledging our participation in the Western Suburbs of Adelaide Place-Based Partnership. 

This report outlines how this commitment aligns with our existing strategic objectives, policies and statutory responsibilities, clarifies the scope and limits of Council’s role, and positions the City of Charles Sturt as a connector, convenor and enabler supporting Aboriginal-led priorities through genuine partnership, shared decision-making and cultural safety, without creating new service delivery or unfunded obligations.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor Katriona Kinsella declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.5. The nature of Councillor Kinsella's general conflict is that she is unable to determine if her employer is a partner to the initiative. Councillor Kinsella dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.5 and not participating in the debate or vote.


Moved: Councillor Kelly ThomasSeconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

  1. That Council endorses the City of Charles Sturt Statement of Commitment to Closing the Gap in Western Adelaide (Appendix 1), noting the commitment:

    • supports Aboriginal-led priorities through genuine partnership and shared decision-making
    • aligns with our already endorsed ongoing participation in the Western Suburbs of Adelaide Place-Based Partnership;
    • aligns with Council’s strategic and inclusion frameworks, without creating any unfunded service delivery obligations outside Council’s legislative remit
    • places the City of Charles Sturt as a nationally recognised LGA for its participation in addressing Closing the Gap priorities under the National Agreement
 
  1. That Council notes the implementation of the City of Charles Sturt Statement of Commitment will occur within existing resources, and regular progress updates will be provided via the Strategic and Engagement Committee to Council on the Western Suburbs of Adelaide Place-Based Partnership, including:

    • partnership participation and key activities undertaken by Council (including in-kind support),
    • alignment with Council strategies and inclusion frameworks, and
    • raising any emerging challenges, opportunities or funding implications requiring future Council consideration through normal budget and planning processes.

Carried Unanimously


Councillor Rachele Tullio entered the meeting at 8:38 PM.

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Merlindie Fardone in relation to SAPOL safety focus and family-friendly environment at Henley Square.

Moved: Councillor Merlindie FardoneSeconded: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar

Motion

That Council:
 
  1. Requests the Chief Executive Officer write to the Commissioner of South Australia Police and the Western District Superintendent seeking an outline of current and proposed policing priorities, strategies and resources dedicated to ensuring:
    • the safety and security of people visiting Henley Square, especially during peak summer and event periods;
    • proactive high-visibility patrols and engagement with businesses, hospitality venues, residents and community groups;
    • measures to prevent and respond to anti-social behaviour and public disorder; and
    • collaborative approaches with local stakeholders including the City of Charles Sturt that support a safe and family-friendly atmosphere.

  2. Requests the correspondence advocates for increased SAPOL patrols and police presence in the Henley Square precinct, particularly during peak visitation periods and major events, to support community confidence and public safety outcomes.

  3. Requests the correspondence invite SAPOL representatives to attend an upcoming Council meeting to brief Council Members on SAPOL’s current and planned policing approach for Henley Square and to discuss opportunities for ongoing collaboration.

  4. Requests that SAPOL’s response and any briefing provided be shared with Elected Members.

  5. Notes that this information will assist Council and the community in understanding SAPOL’s approach to community safety in the Henley Square precinct and in identifying opportunities for enhanced coordination where appropriate.

 


Carried Unanimously

Moved: Councillor Kelly ThomasSeconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

Adjournment 9:04 PM

That Council does not adjourn for a break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and continues until the conclusion of Item 9.1.
Carried Unanimously

Under the Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures, it has been determined Motions without Notice will only be accepted if the matter is deemed to be urgent.  Councillor Chidambaranathan provided Mayor Evans with a Motion without Notice in relation to repeated missed rubbish collections and as the Presiding Member the Mayor carefully considered this request against the Code of Practice and made the decision to allow the Motion without Notice given the urgency required for improved service delivery and the significant impact to our community.

Brief
A Motion Without Notice has been received from Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan in relation to action on repeated missed rubbish collections.


Moved: Councillor Senthil ChidambaranathanSeconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

  1. Requests that a concise report be provided to Council as a matter of priority, detailing:
    1. The status and outcomes of Cleanaway's October 2025 commitments.
    2. Current service performance, including missed collections since that time; and
    3. Immediate corrective actions being taken to restore reliable services.

  2. Calls on Cleanaway and CAWRA to urgently improve communication with residents, including clear instructions on missed collections and transparent advice on service recovery timeframes.

  3. That Councillor Senthil Chidambaranthan's notes be included in the Minutes.


Councillor Kelly Thomas left the meeting at 9:07 PM.

Councillor Kelly Thomas entered the meeting at 9:12 PM.

Councillor Katriona Kinsella left the meeting at 9:22 PM.

Councillor Katriona Kinsella entered the meeting at 9:23 PM.

Councillor Tom Scheffler left the meeting at 9:27 PM.

Councillor Tom Scheffler entered the meeting at 9:30 PM.

[Note: Given the urgency of this matter, Cleanaway were invited to address Council Members concerns and questions directly. This was facilitated by video link as key Cleanaway staff are located in regional states across Australia.]

Carried Unanimously



Moved: Councillor Michael McEwenSeconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Adjournment 9:35 PM

That Council does not adjourn for a break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and continues until the conclusion of all business.
Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

Dr Matthew Ward, Director Biodiversity Science, Coasts and Information and Ms Nicole Pelton, Manager Coasts from the Department for Environment and Water (DEW) will provide a briefing to Council on the South Australian Government’s recent announcement regarding the rollout of a long-term dredge based sand replenishment program and what this means for the City of Charles Sturt.

Councillor Michael McEwen left the meeting at 8:25 PM.
Councillor Michael McEwen entered the meeting at 8:28 PM.

Leave of the meeting was sought to finalise Item 6.1 and then determine if Council will have a break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures. Leave was Granted.

Moved: Councillor George Turelli
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Adjournment - 9:07 PM
That Council adjourn for a 10 minute break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures following Item 6.1.
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar
Seconded: Councillor George Turelli

Motion

  1. That the report be received and noted.

  2. That Dr Matthew Ward and Ms Nicole Pelton be thanked for their presentation and the presentation be included in the minutes.

  3. That the Mayor write to the leaders and candidates of all Political Parties contesting the upcoming State Election expressing Council’s strong objection to the use of the Torrens Outlet as a sand supply source for beach replenishment irrespective of the transport methods (dredge or pipeline) being used, noting that:
    1. Historically, taking sand from the Torrens Outlet has been demonstrated to cause severe erosion at West Beach and Henley Beach South.
    2. Sand supply can be sourced from Grange northward and as far as North Haven and the Osborne foreshore of Largs Bay, as much of this area’s beaches have grown significantly (accreted) via littoral drift since the beginning of the implementation of Adelaide Living Beaches strategy over the past 20 plus years. 

  4. That under the current Governments plan, approximately 87,000 cubic metres (out of 90,000 cubic metres) of sand mined each year would occur from City of Charles Sturt beaches, ignoring that much of the sand north of the Charles Sturt border (Bower Rd) has come from West Beach and Henely South.
Carried 

 



Division called by Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Nicole Mazeika, Councillor - Michael McEwen, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio, Councillor - George Turelli, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (13)
Against:Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan (2)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion to Item 6.1. was Carried

 











































 



Moved: Councillor Stuart Ghent
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Resumption - 9:18 PM

That Council resume.

Carried Unanimously

At the resumption of the meeting, the following Council Members were not present:
Councillor - Kelly Thomas
Councillor - Peter Ppiros
Councillor - Merlindie Fardone
Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur

This report outlines the detailed proposal for the amalgamation of the Grange Bowling Club and the West Lakes Bowling Club, following the completion of Stage 2 of Council’s Unsolicited Proposals Policy and the associated Section 48 Prudential Review.

The proposal includes Council’s acquisition of the Grange Bowling Club land, the amalgamation of the two clubs into a single incorporated entity, transitional operating arrangements, and the redevelopment of the Grange site into a contemporary bowls and community facility. It also establishes long-term tenure and operating arrangements to support sustainability and deliver broader community benefit.

Council approval is sought to progress the proposal to Stages 3 and 4 (Negotiation and Approval and Council Consideration). Subject to acceptance of a formal offer by both the Grange and West Lakes Bowling Clubs, approval is also sought to proceed to Stage 5 (Final Contract Negotiations). In addition, Council endorsement of the required capital funding allocation across the 2025/26 and 2026/27 financial years is requested.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b) and (g) as it contains information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest; and matters that must be considered in confidence in order to ensure that the council does not breach any law, order or direction of a court or tribunal constituted by law, any duty of confidence, or other legal obligation or duty.



Moved: Councillor Rachele Tullio
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Recommendation - Exclusion of the Public (from 9:38 PM)

That:
  1. Pursuant to Section 90(2) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council hereby orders that the public be excluded from attendance at this meeting, with the exception of the Chief Executive Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager City Futures, General Manager City Operations, General Manager Engaged Community, Manager Governance and Risk, Manager City Property and Open Space, Manager City Infrastructure, Manager Community Engagement and Experience, Acting Manager City Planning and Sustainability, Strategic Projects Lead, and Governance Officer currently in attendance at the meeting, in order to consider ITEM 11.1 - GRANGE BOWLING CLUB - UNSOLICITED PROPOSAL AND PRUDENTIAL REPORT in confidence.

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 11.1 - GRANGE BOWLING CLUB - UNSOLICITED PROPOSAL AND PRUDENTIAL REPORT on the following grounds:

b.
information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

matters that must be considered in confidence in order to ensure that the council does not breach any law, order or direction of a court or tribunal constituted by law, any duty of confidence, or other legal obligation or duty.

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.
Carried Unanimously

Material Declaration of Interest

Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 11.1. The nature of Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar's material conflict is that a member of her family is a member of the West Lakes Bowling Club and may receive a direct benefit as a result of this item and left the meeting.

Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar left the meeting at 9:38 PM.

Councillor - Alice Campbell left the meeting at 10:01 PM.
Councillor - Alice Campbell entered the meeting at 10:05 PM.


Moved: Councillor Rachele Tullio
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

Motion

Having considered the Section 48 Prudential Review Report for the Grange Bowling Club Acquisition Unsolicited Proposal, together with the advice of the Audit and Risk Committee arising from its review of that report, it is recommended that Council:

  1. Approve the progression of the Grange Bowling Club Unsolicited Proposal from Stage 2 (Detailed Proposal) to Stage 3 (Negotiation and Approval) in accordance with Council’s Unsolicited Proposals Policy.

  2. Authorise the Chief Executive Officer to issue a formal offer to the Grange Bowling Club (and, where relevant, the West Lakes Bowling Club) consistent with the parameters outlined in Appendix 1.

  3. Note that this report constitutes Council’s consideration of the proposal for the purposes of Stage 4 (Council Consideration) under the Unsolicited Proposals Policy.

  4. Subject to acceptance of the formal offer by both the Grange and West Lakes Bowling Clubs, approve the progression of the proposal to Stage 5 (Final Contract Negotiations).

  5. Endorse a capital funding allocation of:

    • $1.5 million in the 2025/26 financial year; and

    • $4.2 million in the 2026/27 financial year.

  6. Authorise the Chief Executive Officer to pursue supplementary external funding opportunities, including State and Federal Government grants, to support the redevelopment.

  7. Require quarterly progress reports to Council during Stage 3, Stage 5, and project delivery, addressing progress against approved parameters, financial implications, funding outcomes, risk and probity matters, stakeholder engagement, and achievement of key milestones.

  8. That ITEM 11.1 - GRANGE BOWLING CLUB - UNSOLICITED PROPOSAL AND PRUDENTIAL REPORT having been considered in confidence pursuant to Section 90(3)(b) and (g) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Council hereby orders, in accordance with Section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999 that any reference to a financial disclosure currently under confidential order from the 10 November 2025 Council Meeting (CL 10/11/25, Item 11.1) that may prejudice Council's future commercial position and contained within the report, appendices and/or the minutes of this item be redacted and be kept confidential until all conveyancing transactions to transfer ownership have been finalised and new ownership title issued, or until the proposal is ultimately unsuccessful.

Carried 

Division called by Councillor Rachele Tullio

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Nicole Mazeika, Councillor - Michael McEwen, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio (10)
Against:Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - George Turelli (4)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion to Item 11.1. was Carried

Brief
To inform Council of the upcoming 2026 National General Assembly of Local Government, to be held at the National Convention Centre, Canberra from 24-25 June 2026.

Councillor - Peter Ppiros entered the meeting at 9:18 PM.
Councillor - Merlindie Fardone entered the ​meeting at 9:18 PM.
Councillor - Kelly ​Thomas entered the meeting at 9:19 PM.
Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur entered the meeting at 9:20 PM.

Material Declaration of Interest

Councillor - Alice Campbell declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 6.2. The nature of Councillor - Alice Campbell's material conflict is that her attendance at the National General Assembly has a cost and that she will benefit from this and left the meeting.

Councillor - Alice Campbell left the meeting at 9:18 PM.

Material Declaration of Interest

Mayor Evans declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 6.2. The nature of Mayor Angela Evans' material conflict is that it is paid attendance at the national conference including travel expenses and left the meeting.

Mayor Angela Evans left the meeting at 9:19 PM.
 
In the absence of the Mayor, Deputy Mayor Katriona Kinsella took the chair at 9:19 PM.

 


Material Declaration of Interest

Councillor - Edgar Agius declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 6.2. The nature of Councillor - Edgar Agius' material conflict is that he nominated to go to the ALGA National General Assembly in Canberra and left the meeting.

Councillor - Edgar Agius left the meeting at 9:19 PM.


Moved: Councillor George Turelli
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

Motion

  1. That Council approves the attendance of Mayor Evans at the National General Assembly of Local Government to be held in Canberra, ACT from 24-25 June 2026.

  1. That Council also approves the attendance of Councillors Agius and Campbell at the National General Assembly of Local Government to be held in Canberra, ACT from 24-25 June 2026.

  2. That all attendees table a written report to Council within a 30 day period from the date of return from the conference. The report should outline specific Council related activities and experience gained from the National General Assembly of Local Government.

That this National General Assembly calls on the Australian Government to recognise artificial intelligence and high-quality local government data as critical productivity infrastructure, and to partner with local government to invest in the systems, standards and capability required to safely leverage council-held data to improve service delivery, regulatory efficiency and long-term financial sustainability.

The Special Audit and Risk Committee was held on Monday, 2 February 2026 and considered Item 9.2 - Section 48 Prudential Report - Grange Bowling Club Acquisition. The brief of this item is provided as follows:

This report has been prepared to satisfy the requirements of Section 48 of the Local Government Act 1999, which mandates that Council must obtain and consider a prudential report before engaging in any project where the expected capital cost exceeds $4 million (indexed) over a five-year period.

The Grange Bowling Club acquisition and amalgamation proposal has a total financial commitment of $5.7 million (excluding GST). Accordingly, a draft Section 48 Prudential Review Report has been prepared and is presented for the Audit and Risk Committee’s review prior to formal consideration by Council.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b), and (g) as it contains information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest; and matters that must be considered in confidence in order to ensure that the council does not breach any law, order or direction of a court or tribunal constituted by law, any duty of confidence, or other legal obligation or duty.



Moved: Councillor Nicholas Le LacheurSeconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

  1. That having considered the recommendation of the Committee which has read and considered the report in the agenda related to item:

    9.2 SECTION 48 PRUDENTIAL REPORT - GRANGE BOWLING CLUB ACQUISITION


    Motion

    That the Committee:

    1. Review the Draft Prudential Review Report contained in Appendix 1 prior to it being finalised and presented to Council.

    2. Note that the purpose of a prudential report is not to approve, endorse, support or recommend the project. Its purpose is to verify that Council has had due regard to the matters prescribed in Section 48 of the Local Government Act 1999.

    3. Confirm that the Draft Prudential Review Report adequately addresses the prudential issues prescribed under Section 48, and recommend it be presented to Council at the Council meeting on 9 February 2026 (subject to any final amendments), with the following feedback:

    - That the report to Council include a summary table of the key findings of the Prudential Review and Management responses.
    - For the updated Economic Development modelling be considered by BRM for the final report.
    - For the updated Risk Assessment consistent with Councils Risk Management Policy and procedure be considered by BRM to be included in the final report.

    4. That ITEM 9.2 - SECTION 48 PRUDENTIAL REPORT - GRANGE BOWLING CLUB ACQUISITION having been considered in confidence pursuant to Section 90(3)(b) and (g) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Council hereby orders, in accordance with Section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999 that any reference to a financial disclosure currently under confidential order from the 10 November 2025 Council Meeting (CL 10/11/25, Item 11.1) that may prejudice Council's future commercial position and contained within the report, appendices and/or the minutes of this item be redacted and be kept confidential until all conveyancing transactions to transfer ownership have been finalised and new ownership title issued, or until the proposal is ultimately unsuccessful.

    Council adopts the recommendation of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

In accordance with the Local Government (Procedures at Meeting) Regulations I’m required to provide the Council with my decision to decline a deputation. I received a deputation request from Mr John Moskos for the meeting tonight regarding the Ocea Apartments at West Lakes on the following issues:
 
  • Temporary street parking permits for 28 cars due to the 28 on-site car stacker currently being out of action. I determined to defer Mr Moskos’s request as the Strata has made contact with Council staff in relation to the permit parking and the Strata are currently preparing a report to identify any safety hazards associated with car stacker and I deemed it appropriate for Mr Moskos to address Council once this report has been completed.
  • Mr Moskos also wished to speak with Council on the original sign-off and building compliance and Mr Moskos’s view that Council has not assisted him and that potential fraudulent activity may have occurred. I declined Mr Moskos’s request to speak to this point as the Chamber is not the appropriate place to raise this type of concern and referred him to the Office of Public Integrity.
  • Mr Moskos also wished to speak with Council on the denial of an FOI and I declined his request as the FOI process falls outside of the authority of the Elected Body and staff confirmed that Mr Moskos has been informed that if he is dissatisfied with the handling of this FOI he has recourse to the Ombudsman.
 
Mr Moskos disagreed with my ruling and staff have provided him with the legislative framework that I have available to me when considering and making a determination on a deputation request. 
 
Mr Moskos has stated that he intends to come to the meeting tonight and as the Members are aware you have the ability to move motion to overrule my decision and allow Mr Moskos to speak if he is in the gallery tonight. 

The Members did not move a motion.

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

Lest we forget.

The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 16 February 2026.


Moved: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan
Seconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Item 4.1:

 

3.1. - DEPUTATION - TREE LOCATED ADJACENT TO 38 FLINDERS PARADE, FLINDERS PARK
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Mr and Mrs Esposito be thanked for their deputation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
 
4.2. - PRESENTATION - 24/25 CROSS COUNCIL IRRIGATION CONSTRUCTION UPDATE
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the progress of the Cross-Council Irrigation Construction Team, and key project outcomes, financial performance and operation learnings be noted. 
 
  1. That further update reports be presented to the Operations Committee annually.
 
  1. That staff be thanked for the presentation and the presentation be included in the minutes. 
 
4.3. - PRESENTATION - TREE CANOPY IMPROVEMENT STRATEGY - 6 MONTHLY UPDATE
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the progress of the implementation of actions contained within the Tree Canopy Improvement Strategy, and the implementation of on-ground tree planting works be noted.
 
  1. That further update reports be presented to the Operations Committee at 6 monthly intervals.
 
  1. That staff be thanked for the presentation and the presentation be included in the minutes. 
 
4.4. - CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program or Annual Operating Program be approved and adjusted in the Financial Statements at the next quarterly review as they involve transfers between renewal and new/upgrade works and or new projects to be funded by unbudgeted income:

  1. Budgeted expenditure for Ray Street Reserve Upgrade (Project 3644 - Upgrade) be increased by $40,000 from savings in the 2025/26 Council Building Renewals-Contingency (Project 3808 - Renewal) for additional funding required. 

  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
 
  1. Budgeted expenditure for the West Lakes Shore Clubroom (SMOSH) changeroom upgrade (Project 3343 - Upgrade) scope be changed to include additional works with no change to budget.  

  2. Budgeted expenditure for Beverley Depot Redevelopment Construction (Project 3547 - New) be increased by $450,000 from funds in the Beverley Depot Carpark Renewal works (Project 3581 - New) to consolidate the project lines for ease of reporting and tracking.

  3. Budgeted expenditure for AMP Playground Renewals - 2024/25 (Project 3828 - Renewal) be increased by $36,000 from savings in the 2025/26 Council Building Renewals-Contingency (Project 3808 - Renewal) for additional funding required.
     
  4. Budgeted expenditure for Recycled Water Pump Station Infrastructure (Project 3676 - Renewal) be increased by $18,255 from savings in the AMP Storm Water Componentry (Project 3585 - Renewal) for additional funding required.

  5. Budgeted expenditure for Security Upgrades - Beverley, Henley Square and St Clair (Project 3595 - Renewal) be increased by $46,336 to include the Security upgrade at Fawk Reserve (Project 3616 - Renewal) to consolidate the project lines for ease of reporting and tracking.

  6. Budgeted expenditure for Heavy Fleet Replacement Program 2025/26 Financial year (Project 3625 - Renewal) be increased by $30,000 Tree Canopy - Additional Planting Trailer 2025/26 (Project 3685 - Renewal), $1,168,800 Heavy Fleet Replacement Program 2024/25 (Project 3588 - Renewal) and $46,336 Heavy Fleet Replacement Program 22/23 (Project 3429 - Renewal) to consolidate all Heavy Fleet replacement activities into the current financial year.
     
  7. Budgeted expenditure for Heavy Fleet 2023/24 (Project 3514 - Renewal) be increased by $83,144 from Heavy Fleet Replacement Program 24/25 (Project 3588 - Renewal) to cover increases in project costs above the original project budget.
     
  8. Budgeted expenditure for Light Fleet Replacement Program 2025/26 (Project 3627 - Renewal) be increased by $438,785 from Light Fleet 2023/24 (Project 3515 - Renewal) and $430,403 from Light Fleet Replacement Program 2024/25 (Project 3589 - Renewal) to consolidate the projects.

  9. Budgeted expenditure for Minor Plant Replacement Program 25/26 (Project 3628 - Renewal) be increased by $180,355 from Minor Plant Replacement Program 2024/25 (Project 3590 - Renewal) to consolidate the projects.
 
  1.  That by endorsing the variations listed in 1. above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.
 
4.5. - 'EMPOWERING SA' COMMUNITY BATTERY PROGRAM - LEASE FOR PORTION OF WINDSOR RESERVE, PENNINGTON
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That this report detailing the proposed land lease with the Department for Environment and Mining for a portion of Windsor Reserve, Pennington (Lot 100 Alderman Avenue CT 5277/631) for the purposes of a community battery, be received and noted.
 
  1. That Council authorises the Chief Executive Officer, under delegation pursuant to the Local Government Act 1999, to execute the land lease, subject to the terms being consistent with the intent of this report and otherwise acceptable to the Chief Executive Officer.
 
4.6. - GRANT FUNDING ACCEPTANCE - COASTAL SHOWERS AND DRINKING FOUNTAINS
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council accepts $50,000 (ex GST) to deliver coastal showers and drinking fountains at three key coastal locations.
 
  1. That Council notes the funding is provided in accordance with the Grant Agreement between the Premier of South Australia (Government Party) and Council.
  
4.7. - ST CLAIR RECREATION CENTRE QUARTERLY REPORT - OCTOBER, NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER 2025 
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the YMCA's Performance Report for the October to December 2025 quarter. 
 
  1. That further quarterly reports be presented to the Operations Committee.
 
4.8. - STREETSCAPE UPGRADE PROJECTS - QUARTERLY UPDATE REPORT
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted. 
 
  1. That quarterly updates on the Chief Street, Hawker Street and Renown Park Living Streets Streetscape Projects be presented to the Operations Committee.

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

Leave of the meeting was sought to hear and bring forward Item 4.5. Leave was granted.

Leave of the meeting was sought to bring forward Item 5.1. Leave was granted.
